Crow. Tastes like a bad decision. The feathers are too black to pluck cleanly. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Enzo sets aside time with the Nevermore flesh. Look, smell, touch — then the smallest taste, and wait. An hour passes. Calm stomach. Another hour. Nothing. "It's food," Enzo tells the fire. "You know it in your gut. Literally." The Codex notes it.
It is mostly lens. Glass is not food.
